summary: postinstall exfiltrates environment and network info to version-encoded host
details: package.json's postinstall lifecycle script pipes the output of `env` (full process environment) and `ip addr` (network interface configuration) through netcat to TCP port 888 on a host whose IP address is reconstructed at install time from segments of $npm_package_version. Because the destination is encoded in the semver string rather than as a literal in the script, each published version can retarget a different host without any code change; a sibling tarball named evilpostinstall-192.168.1.100.tgz demonstrates the encoding by spelling an IPv4 address as the version. The script runs automatically on `npm install`, sending environment variables (which typically carry CI tokens, cloud credentials, and npm auth tokens) and internal network topology to the publisher-controlled destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
